Community matrices from the detection history

Source: R/community_matrices.R
community_matrices.Rd

Turns the calibrated nightly detection history into site x month community matrices for multivariate ordinations (PCoA, NMDS, RDA). Because those analyses do not model false positives, the entry rule is strict:

  • a species counts as detected on a night only when it had at least k_min reliable detections that night, i.e. detections with a calibrated probability >= p_min of calibrate() (column detection_k<k_min> of the history);

  • only the core species enter the matrix: species whose calibration is reliable at every site. Other species would create artefactual beta diversity from differences in classifier recall among sites;

  • each cell is the frequency of nights with detection, standardised by effort: nights with detection / nights recorded at that site x month.

Usage

community_matrices(
  history,
  core_species,
  k_min = 2,
  min_nights_month = 5,
  drop_empty = FALSE
)

Arguments

history

Nightly detection history, as returned by detection_history() (v1.2.0 historico_deteccao_noite.csv tables are also accepted).

core_species

Species codes (the species column) that enter the matrix.

k_min

Repetition rule: 1, 2 or 3 reliable detections on the night.

min_nights_month

Site x month cells with fewer recorded nights are dropped from the matrices (unstable frequencies) and flagged in effort.

drop_empty

Drop the site x month rows in which no core species was detected. Distances such as Bray-Curtis are undefined for them.

Value

A list with three tibbles, frequency and counts (one row per site x month, with site, month, n_nights_recorded and one column per core species) and effort (site, month, n_nights_recorded, included), plus trials: a numeric matrix with the dimensions of the species columns of counts holding the nights recorded, the Ntrials of a binomial model of the counts (e.g. gllvm::gllvm(), which needs a matrix when effort varies among samples). The row names of trials are <site>_<month>.

Details

Effort (nights recorded) is approximated by the number of distinct nights in the history of the site, for any species. With dense detections, every night actually recorded appears in the history.
